sections.title: One Single Flash vs. Ongoing Rhythm
sections.content: Hungarian derivational morphology pairs verbs of sensory perception, sound, and movement into micro-systems that distinguish a single instantaneous event (semelfactive, marked by -int/-ant or -an/-en) from a continuous or repeated series (marked by -og/-eg/-ög or -gat/-get). For example: pillant ('casts a single glance') vs. pillantgat / nézeget ('glances repeatedly'); koppan ('makes a single thud/knock') vs. kopog / kopogtat ('knocks repeatedly'); megbillen ('tilts once') vs. billeget ('tilts back and forth').

sections.title: Sensory Precision in Narrative Prose
sections.content: Writers like Tamási Áron rely on these pairs to bring scenes to life without heavy adverbial modifiers. Instead of writing 'he touched the string once lightly', Hungarian says megpendítette a húrt; instead of 'he kept strumming the strings', it says pengette a húrokat. Choosing between instantaneous and iterative suffixes gives your B2 narrative prose unmistakable native texture.

sections.title: Instantaneous (Semelfactive) vs. Continuous/Iterative Pairs
rows: pillant (casts one glance) <-> nézeget / pillantgat (glances repeatedly)
Egyetlen pillantást vetett rá vs. Sokáig nézegette.
Egy fenyőtoboz koppant a tetőn vs. Valaki kopogtatott az ajtón.
Villant egyet a fejsze éle vs. A távolban fények villogtak.
Megcsörrent a kulcs a zárban vs. A szél csörgette a száraz leveleket.

items.spanish: Ábel csak egyszer pillantott vissza a völgyre, mielőtt belépett a sűrű fenyvesbe.
items.english: Ábel glanced back at the valley only once before stepping into the dense pine forest.

items.spanish: Valaki halkan bekopogtatott a kunyhó havas ablakán az éjszaka közepén.
items.english: Someone knocked softly several times on the snowy window of the hut in the middle of the night.

items.spanish: A parázs hirtelen felvillant a sötétben, majd újra csendesen izzott tovább.
items.english: The ember suddenly flared up once in the dark, then glowed on quietly again.

items.spanish: Az őszi szél egész éjjel zörgette a zsindelytetőt a fejünk felett.
items.english: All night long the autumn wind kept rattling the shingle roof above our heads.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Remember: '-an/-en' and '-ant/-int' mark a single split-second event ('villan', 'koppan', 'pillant'), while '-og/-eg/-ög' and '-gat/-get' stretch the action into a series ('villog', 'kopogtat', 'zörget').
